contest: Americans Against Gun Violence National High School Essay Contest 2020

criteria.name: answers_prompt
criteria.reason: Takes a clear position in line one of the thesis, "A ban on handguns and assault weapons is the most effective way to reduce firearm-related injuries," and backs it with three harms. It never addresses the strongest objection (rights, enforcement, existing guns), so 'describe your thoughts' is argued only one way.

criteria.name: specificity
criteria.reason: Cited numbers ("nearly 40,000," "1 million women... shot at them," "3 out of 4 children"), a named case (Katie Stubblefield) and one unfakeable personal detail ("which cabinets I can fit in"). The state comparison stays vague: "somewhat effective," "fewest numbers."

criteria.name: human_voice
criteria.reason: Tells found: "does not just plague schools" (not-just construction), the cliché "permanent solution for a temporary problem," "It is clear that," signpost chain "Further... Finally," and the stock "ironically" list. The opening classroom paragraph sounds like a real person, and no em dashes appear.

criteria.name: stories
criteria.reason: Two beats: the writer's own lockdown-drill habit (on topic but abandoned after paragraph 1) and the Stubblefield case (told in three summary sentences, no scene). The body runs on statistics, not story.

criteria.name: ideas_mechanism
criteria.reason: Shows why the existing fix fails in one place: storage fails because "3 out of 4 children... know where it is located." Elsewhere it jumps to the ban without a mechanism: "It is clear that current background checks do not catch these abusive individuals and the only way... is to implement a ban." The essay also never says how a ban would work or who would carry it out.

criteria.name: structure_ending
criteria.reason: Clear thesis-and-three-points shape, but the close never returns to the classroom. It ends on a restatement: "including the bans on handguns and assault weapons that the American Academy of Pediatrics recommended two decades ago."

fixes: Word limit (-10, recovers all 10): at 649 words the essay is 149 over the 500 limit. Cut the whole moon/world-wide-web/COVID paragraph (about 110 words), and in paragraph 2 cut the sentence "In order to address these horrendous numbers, some states have enacted limited gun control laws that have been somewhat effective." Then close in 2 to 3 sentences of your own (see fix 3).

Voice (+8 possible): rewrite "However, gun violence does not just plague schools." as a plain statement, e.g. "Schools are where I learned to fear guns, but most gun injuries happen at home." Replace "A lethal device that creates a permanent solution for a temporary problem" with a plain claim about the tripled suicide risk you already cite. Delete "It is clear that" and "ironically", and swap "Further"/"Finally" for direct topic sentences.

Ending and mechanism (+4 structure, +6 ideas): end with the real cabinets and escape routes from your opening, e.g. what a ban would mean for that drill, rather than restating the AAP. In the domestic-violence paragraph, replace "the only way... is to implement a ban" with one sentence on why background checks miss abusers. Use only a reason you can cite; if you have no source, cut the claim rather than make one up.
